text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- 10 Toronto hospitals to be closed: Commission expects savings of C$430 million; proposes C$50-million for replacement care.
- Eaton's return dividend to chain: Creditors pleased to see C$10 million.
- Yeltsin tackles familiar targets: Russian President criticizes NATO, fat-cat bureaucracy on return to parliament.
- B.C.'s fiscal wrist slapped by Moody's: Bond rater dislikes surprise deficits.
- Queen takes to the Web: Monarch announces new site to Ontario students by E-mail.
- Philip snaps up 2 U.S. firms: Environmental company becomes North American giant with US$612-million deal.
- Hudson's Bay profit doubles in quarter: Retailer sharp contrast to Eaton's as cost cutting gives a boost.
- Credit card operation no sinkhole for Eaton's: Unit saw a C$55-million profit, but is out of creditors' grasp.
- An oil boom dawns on Newfoundland.
- Shaw takes out death star rival: Buying 50 percent of Star Choice to speed up satellite TV launch.
- Eaton's to open its books: Family returns C$10-million dividend as veil starts to lift on financial secrecy.
- US$540-million deal for Allwaste makes Philip Environmental king of waste heap.
